brief: Goldman's TMT morning note (Bartlett, FICC & Equities) covers a quiet futures tape after NDX's Friday ATH. Schneider Electric's ~$22.6bn all-cash bid for PTC (+36%) lifts ADSK/PCOR in sympathy; Musk's Terafab talks with TSMC lift TSM and pressure INTC. Brazil's EWZ jumps 13% pre-market as Bolsonaro's surprise runoff lead offsets France/Spain fiscal risk, which pushed the Euro to a 17-month low and widened France-Germany spreads. GS's semis desk turns more constructive into 3Q earnings after a sector pullback (SOX -11% vs SPX +4%) drove de-risking, flagging upside in SemiCap/analog/memory (long AMAT/STX/MCHP, short QCOM/KLAC/WDC) on WFE pull-ins and hyperscaler capex; SIA data shows above-seasonal August shipments. Prime Services shows US L/S net leverage at five-year lows even as equities were net bought via short covering in Macro Products; Russell 2000 futures positioning sits near record-short, and softer payrolls/PCE data have eased rate expectations and sparked covering, though sustained RTY outperformance requires durable rate relief first. The desk debates fully re-committing to the AI trade given rates/oil/midterm uncertainty. Separately, GS previews Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% (vs 33% in Q2), with AI infrastructure beneficiaries driving over half of that growth; Adobe stays Sell despite new CEO, Z.AI upgraded to Buy.
